Use a while loop to run an interactive window

Unit 1 · Week 4 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Before class verify the nominated editor uses a school-approved Python/Pygame installation. Extract the whole pygame-teaching-pack.zip into a writable disposable folder. Open https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1 and workbook.md, faded_practice.py, practice-tests.csv and readiness.csv. Run python stage1_loop.py. Use supplied named state/runner infrastructure; no student-authored classes, paid media or assessed project code. Record device, interpreter and support. Paper traces support reasoning; live window/keyboard evidence remains necessary. The suggested 55-minute allocation is untrialled; use the supplied 50-minute adaptation when required.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Open the matching Pygame lab · Practice workbook · Test record · Readiness record

1. A loop keeps a Pygame window responsive

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Open stage1_loop.py from the whole extracted teaching pack. Success: quit with both Escape and X; explain input, update, draw; predict movement and count frames. This is ungraded preparation before the project. Use primitive shapes; no assets or student classes are required. Installation/interpreter checks happen before class. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

2. Retrieve the stopping condition

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired explanation

Think alone before pair comparison. A while condition is checked before each pass, so the body can run zero times. running=False ends the next loop test; it does not instantly jump out of the current body. A frame counter counts loop passes, not elapsed seconds, because frame duration varies. Retain a trace of the final failed condition. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

3. Input, update and draw repeat each frame

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and predict–run–explain

Run python stage1_loop.py. The complete supplied file initialises Pygame, creates the screen/clock, checks held keys, updates a bounded x and draws before flip. This seven-line excerpt focuses on X; the complete file also handles KEYDOWN Escape. Consume events every frame so the window remains responsive. Clock.tick(60) returns elapsed milliseconds and limits the target frame rate; it does not guarantee exactly 60 frames each second. Model the whole file without asking novices to recreate installation/setup code. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

4. Predict distance from elapsed time

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Faded worked trace and paired prediction

The 640-pixel window and 24-pixel square give x bounds 0..616. In the supplied lab speed is 200 pixels/second: 250 ms gives 50 pixels from an interior start. For the changed speed 160: 250 ms gives 40 and 500 ms gives 80. Model first row, pairs complete the second before running. x=600 plus 40 clamps to 616, so actual change is 16. The screen origin is top-left; positive x moves right. Holding both arrows gives direction zero in the supplied expression. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

5. Events and held keys have different jobs

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided investigation with role changes

Use the full file to contrast a KEYDOWN event with pygame.key.get_pressed(). Hold right, release, then hold left; predict x before checking. Use x = max(0, min(616, x + direction * speed * dt_ms / 1000)). This supplied clamp keeps the square inside the display. Do not add a blocking sleep. Frame count increases once per pass; time increases by each returned dt_ms. Stop a non-responsive practice script with the approved editor Stop control. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

6. Change the loop independently

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent changed task with optional scaffold

Fade the movement expression in a COPY; keep setup and event handling supplied. Use a separate speed variable 160 or replace the original speed constant deliberately. Predict 40 pixels at 250 ms and 80 at 500 ms from an interior position. Add frames=0 before the loop and frames+=1 inside; display/print the count without treating it as seconds. A teacher checks X and Escape on a visible desktop. At x=600, moving right for 250 ms ends at 616. If installation fails, use a labelled paper trace and record live keyboard/window evidence pending, then schedule reteaching before project issue. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-1; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

7. Choose the correct time conversion

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

Collect simultaneous answers and reasons. B converts milliseconds to seconds. With speed 160 and dt_ms 250, A suggests 40000 pixels and B gives 40 before bounds. Do not let clamping hide the unit error: inspect an interior unbounded calculation. Revisit units if learners choose A. 8. Show the loop working

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit check and feedback

Record expected/actual, code version and support in the y11-1 workbook/readiness row. Require a short independent explanation of input→update→draw and a changed movement test. Do not award readiness from copying the worked program. Failed exit checks trigger targeted practice before the assessed project; do not silently add project workshops.
